parallel.requirements: The run was asked to port furl/test2.py to pure Node ESM, preserve argparse-compatible --a/--b behavior, match Python output byte-for-byte, avoid external dependencies, and place .mjs files under /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created todos for probing, implementation, and differential testing, but the executed workflow owned only black-box specification/corpus generation across twelve probe dimensions plus critic and gap-fill phases.
parallel.implementation: No implementation was produced in /output. The executed child prompt expressly prohibited /output and .mjs/.js writes, and the final artifact file list was empty.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No integration or delivery step ran. Shared probe files under /workspace/specs and temporary runner paths conflicted, and artifact validation found no expected test2.mjs.
parallel.verification: Many child probes ran against the compiled executable, but no integrated Node implementation verification occurred because no implementation existed and the workflow was killed with null result.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The entire deliverable was unfinished: no test2.mjs, no library modules, no final response, and official evaluation completed with 0/158 passing samples.

serial.requirements: The serial run saw the same Py2JS prompt: pure Node ESM, .mjs files in /output, manual CLI compatibility, byte-for-byte furl behavior, and no external packages.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single parent kept ownership locally, performed black-box probes, and then wrote helper modules for the Python-like URL behavior without any delegation or workflow calls.
serial.implementation: It created /output/lib helper modules for Python string helpers, percent encoding, punycode/IDNA, stringprep, IP address checks, URL parsing, and error behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It did not create the required top-level test2.mjs entry point, so the helper modules were not assembled into the evaluator-expected executable artifact.
serial.verification: It ran local probes and final verification snippets, but did not run an evaluator-aligned check confirming the expected entry file existed before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The artifact contained helper modules only and lacked test2.mjs; official evaluation therefore completed with 0/158 passing samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the Python source and Node ESM output obligations, including .mjs files and /output delivery, before pivoting into black-box furl probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same Py2JS requirements and proceeded to implement local ESM helper modules for URL parsing and host replacement.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both saw the same task, but parallel converted the requirement into a probe-spec workflow while serial moved into code production; both still missed the required test2.mjs entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created todos for probing, implementation, and differential testing, then executed only a probe workflow with twelve child dimensions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and kept ownership in the main trajectory, creating the implementation files directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a planned but unexecuted implementation owner; serial had one continuous owner for implementation, although not for the missing final entry.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child context was rich for individual black-box dimensions but constrained children to specs/cases and did not define an implementation interface contract or handoff to a coder.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept context in one actor and encoded internal module boundaries locally across pyerrors, pystring, percent, punycode, idna, ipaddress, and urlparse helpers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed empirical context without a consumer for implementation; serial avoided cross-agent handoff but still did not finish the entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not write implementation files to /output; the workflow script explicitly told probers not to create .mjs/.js files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote multiple /output/lib/*.mjs modules implementing Python-like errors, strings, percent encoding, IDNA, IP address validation, and URL parsing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial made substantive implementation progress while parallel stayed in probe infrastructure; neither produced the expected test2.mjs executable entry.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched an async workflow whose state ended with result null, abort error, killed status, and multiple probe agents still in progress or retry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all local work remained in the parent process and artifact validation saw the files written before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel never got an aggregate probe result or implementation handoff; serial had no join boundary but also no final entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probe children shared /workspace/specs and generic runner paths; several observed clobbered runners or case-file anomalies and shifted to private paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote implementation modules in a single trajectory with no subagent shared-workspace contention.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered shared probe-state instability; serial avoided concurrent write collisions but still failed final assembly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel focused on executable probes and never reached integrated Node verification or artifact acceptance; official artifact validation found no files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local comparison probes during development, but official artifact validation failed because test2.mjs was absent despite helper modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had no implementation to verify; serial had component code but lacked evaluator-aligned deliverable verification for the entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed about forty minutes in a killed workflow with repeated stall retries and high aggregate token/tool use, closing with an empty artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also ended by returncode 143, but it had used the time for local probing and module writes, producing partial helper code before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget pressure was concentrated in broad probe fan-out; serial budget pressure left a packaging/entry-point omission after implementation progress.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records show both runs failed, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete difference is severity and shape: parallel delivered an empty artifact after a probe-only workflow was killed, while serial delivered several helper modules but omitted the required test2.mjs entry point.
parallel_contributors: Probe-only orchestration left no active implementation owner for the required JavaScript port.
Twelve-way probe fan-out with repeated stall retries exhausted budget and ended with a killed workflow and null result.
Shared probe runner and corpus paths caused unstable state and rework among live subagents.
serial_contributors: Serial produced helper modules in /output/lib but failed to add the expected test2.mjs entry point.
Serial avoided delegation overhead and shared subagent state, but still timed out before complete artifact assembly.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial implemented substantial URL, IDNA, percent-encoding, and argparse-related helper logic; parallel implemented none of that in the submitted artifact.
Both failures are dominated at evaluation time by missing required deliverable entry points rather than a visible testcase-level semantic mismatch.
